A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SAEmnesia, with the same authors, core method and substantial shared experiments. Text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v2 reports original UnlearnCanvas experiments, classification and loss analyses, sequential unlearning, adversarial evaluations and I2P nudity-removal results.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds style erasure, held-out concept evaluation, black-box attacks, SDXL-Turbo experiments and computational measurements.

M1.justification: The supervised concept-latent assignment, TopK SAE, reconstruction/assignment/decorrelation/sparsity losses and latent-steering procedure remain unchanged. The two-latent nudity variant already appears in v2. v3 describes applying existing score-based selection to unseen concepts without introducing a distinct algorithmic component.

E1.justification: v3 adds style erasure and sequential style erasure to the existing object-erasure and nudity tasks (Appendix A.15). Styles were already training labels in v2, but were not evaluated as erasure targets. Ring-A-Bell additionally introduces a black-box adversarial prompt scenario beyond the retained white-box evaluation.

E2.justification: SalUn is added to the main object comparison in Table 1, although it already appeared in v2's adversarial figure. Conversely, v2 Figure 9's nine non-SAE adversarial comparators disappear from the corresponding v3 comparison, which retains SAeUron. New Table 12 compares against an untouched model and Surkov et al.'s unsupervised SAE on SDXL-Turbo.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 replaces the stated training templates with one-sentence anchor prompts and identifies templates as test prompts. The reported two-latent nudity multiplier changes from -60 to -600 (v2 Table 9; v3 Table 13); neither revision establishes a rerun. New protocols include training on half the styles and testing the remainder, six-style sequential erasure, Ring-A-Bell using seven prompt pairs per object, SDXL-Turbo evaluation without CRA, and timing ten images.

E4.justification: v3 adds tests of generalization beyond supervised concepts, black-box attack robustness, sequential style-erasure scalability and a training/inference cost breakdown. These address substantive questions absent from v2. Existing loss variants, Cats-Dogs overlap counts, class-interference heatmaps, k-NN validation and multiplier analyses are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: The four-seed accuracy mean-and-standard-deviation analysis is unchanged (v2 Table 2; v3 Table 5). Additional timing tables extend the use of ± summaries to new results without specifying a new uncertainty estimator or significance procedure. The ten-image timing sample does not establish an increase in accuracy-evaluation runs.

E6.justification: White-box before/after UA changes from 73.30/28.30 to 97.60/57.50 for SAEmnesia and from 26.19/2.22 to 83.70/34.20 for SAeUron (v2 Figure 9 and text; v3 Table 2). These are unexplained replacements, not established same-setting gains. v3 adds style, sequential-style, held-out, black-box, SDXL-Turbo and timing results; examples include style averages of 98.19 versus 98.10 and held-out averages of 73.75 versus 72.32. Existing main object scores and nudity detection counts remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(11), including the concept score, centralization condition, supervised losses, intervention rule and alternative cross-entropy loss, retain their mathematical substance. Parameter-symbol changes are not new definitions or derivations. Neither version adds formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v3 materially recalibrates the headline performance claim: the 9.22-point object advantage is explicitly over the SAE baseline, while SalUn has the higher object-only average, 94.28 versus 91.51. It adds a claim of best combined object/style performance at 94.85. The centralization contribution, search reduction and nine-object sequential advantage remain.

C2.justification: New Section 5 discusses transformer adaptation, unseen concepts, within-group interference and vocabulary-capacity limits. Appendix A.13 qualifies SDXL-Turbo findings through classifier domain mismatch, and the adversarial mechanism explanation becomes an explicit hypothesis. New style interpretations sometimes overstate the evidence: A.15 claims matching or improving every metric despite slightly lower IRA and CRA in Table 14.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies TopK k=32, expansion factor 16, Adam, learning rate 5×10^-6, batch size 128, A100 hardware, and a 27-configuration loss-weight search using validation loss over five epochs. It adds timing/resource information and a source-code location. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation without establishing changes to previously undisclosed settings. The earlier disclosure of corrected SAeUron metric computation is removed.

R1.justification: Section 2 replaces the historical and concept-resurgence overview with expanded positioning against methods including RECE, SLUG, ConceptPrune and ScaPre. New experiments introduce Ring-A-Bell and Surkov et al.'s SAE work. Several earlier citations, including Cao and Yang and the resurgence studies, disappear. The changes exceed bibliographic updates and accompany narrower claims relative to SAE-based competitors.

P1.justification: v3 rewrites selected abstract, related-work, setup and results passages, updates author information and terminology, introduces dedicated Limitations and Impact Statement sections, and moves hyperparameter discussion earlier in the appendix. Most method exposition and existing analysis prose and ordering remain recognizable; the added scientific material does not constitute wholesale rewriting.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a conference layout with running headers and a single-column appendix, redraws Figure 2, reformats the main comparison table, and replaces the adversarial bar chart with Table 2. It combines v2 Figures 10–12 into Figure 9's panels, adds a style-erasure image grid and several tables, and relocates/resizes existing grids, heatmaps and multiplier plots.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially improves claim calibration and reproducibility: adding SalUn corrects v2's broad object-performance claim, newly disclosed training/search details make replication more feasible, and held-out tests plus explicit limitations address important gaps in evaluating supervised concept mappings. Unexplained adversarial-score replacements, narrower attack comparisons and overstatements around Tables 12 and 14 remain weaknesses. Nevertheless, the more complete comparison and clearer account of implementation and applicability provide a substantial net quality gain.
